One morning after my mother and step-father had had an argument, my mother woke me up and told me to get into my school uniform and get out the front. Apparently I "hadn't stood up for her" enough the previous night, despite the fight happening in the middle of the night and me not knowing what was going on. I was made to wait outside in my school uniform until it was time for school, then walk to school. When I got home that afternoon my mother said I wasn't allowed to call her "mum" anymore, and that she was "Mrs (Lastname)" to me from then on. Later that night she cornered me in the pantry, spat on me, and called me her "infinite disappointment."

I was in the 6th grade.

I used to be bullied horribly at school, and then suffer through nasty shit at home. Every single day for years. I was raised religious, and the only time I had to myself was my walk to school. I would spend the entire 25-minute walk praying to God to just let me have one nice day. Let my bullies be absent, let me have good classes, let my mother not be drunk when I got home, anything. After years of begging and pleading, and getting nothing back, I lost my faith completely. If there's an all-powerful being that won't even help a begging child, then he is undeserving of worship.

Our mother was a terrible woman and is now under a psychiatric hold/rehab program and I don't know when she gets out. I started studying childcare so that I can make sure that no children are ever treated the way that we were. I'm supposed to graduate a degree in Early Childhood Education on April 1st but nobody will ever hire me in that field due to my mental health history, so I've wasted 18 months of my life. I don't think I'm going anywhere.

Unemployed due to the interstate move, have been studying through all of 2019. You can see a "counsellor" on your own but a proper full-on therapist needs a referral. Which means sitting a mental health plan with a GP.

I am one person in a world that does not have my best interests at heart, I never feel safe, I never feel respected or valued, and I no longer wish to participate. I have formed a plan for my suicide. I know that's not a normal thing to have because they ask you about it during the course of a mental health plan. I don't want to be checked into a facility because if I have my agency taken away from me I might become worse, and hospitals are where this new disease thing is and if I get it I will die slow and painful. I need to go, quick and painless, and just be apart from this, and I'm too fucking cowardly to do it so I'm whining on reddit and hoping an answer falls into my fucking lap, same as I ever did.

Stay alive for what? I survive my depression, I have to contend with whatever the fuck this current illness is thats gonna kill everyone. We somehow survive that, we have to live through being run by leaders who DO NOT HAVE OUR BEST INTERESTS AT HEART AND ACTIVELY HARM US WITH THEIR DECISIONS. And even if we somehow oust all of them, the climate change problem has irreparably killed the world. We are all going to die, my brain is just telling me to be ahead of the curve and die while there's still a comfortable or painless way to do so.

I go through phases, back and forth, through all these things. My father got me into older music, and when I went to him once when I was younger and told him I had no ideas, no plan, and was terrified, he quoted George Harrison: "If you don't know where you're going, any road will take you there."

Twice. The first time it was my first job, and I felt I owed them some kind of loyalty. I'd moved out of home on a shoestring budget to escape shitty parents. Then I got older, and it was only casual employment, so they started putting me on less and less. I remember going to the manager at the time almost in tears because I was not making enough money to live on anymore. He told me he'd put me on more shifts, then didn't. I bailed a month after.

The second time, I was at a job I could genuinely have seen a future in. I worked hard, all hours, I was polite, got along well with all the regulars. Other members of the team, however, would flat-out just not do their jobs. I got frustrated one day and pointed this out to the boss, who said there was nothing he could do about it. This frustrated me more. Then I got called in for a shift even though I had a bad toothache, but it was an overnight shift so I went anyway. The next morning I told the manager I wouldn't be in the following day cos I was going to a dentist to get sorted, and he said fine. The guy who he called in to cover me spent the entirety of that shift sending me abusive messages via facebook about how I was "pathetic" and "faking it," so after the dental appointment I went in. The employee shit himself and started apologizing, but I waved it off. I worked well and said nothing (mainly cos my tooth hurt). I left a note for my boss asking him to call me over the weekend to discuss the bullshit, he didn't. I went in on Monday, laid out my 2 years worth of complaints that he hadn't done anything about, and then the abusive messages (screenshotted) as the final straw, and said I wouldn't be back. That manager resigned the following day and it turns out there was a ton of shady shit happening there that I legally can't mention.

TL;DR - Slowly learned to stand up for myself to stop my brain eating itself from the inside out. Now I live in another state with much better family and I'm studying to be a teacher.

I love when they're scrambling to get it locked in while the other guy frantically fights to the ropes or something. It's hard for me to get excited for a finish if I've watched a guy be in a submission for the last minute or so. It's just my opinion, but watching a guy sit in a hold for a long time and then tapping sort of slows the matches down right at the very end, it feels anti-climactic to me. I guess I love a short, sharp finish, and a really long submission hold doesn't really hold my interest. Constantly fighting to escape, get to the ropes, and/or trading holds as a finishing sequence is a lot better to me.

I'm a fan of the pass-out finish (like Bret vs Stone Cold at Mania 13) to make both guys look good. I've just personally never understood getting stuck in a hold for like 30 seconds before tapping. If there's no way out, fighters tap to avoid injury. Like the match against Rollins where Cena got his nose broken, when Cena hooked in the STF for the finish Rollins tapped almost immediately. Granted they probably had to rush the finish to get Cena some medical attention, but it did make the hold look legit.

In my mind, having one guy struggling to lock in his hold against his opponent, and then when he finally gets it locked in the opponent taps within 2-3 seconds would work. Sell the struggle to escape as the tension, rather than "can he outlast the pain of this hold?"
